# A genuinely TWO-COLUMN page, for the coordinate-sort pass.
#
# This is the case the reading-order pass exists for, and the case that is
# indistinguishable from the exam table on geometry alone unless the
# discriminators in detectReadingColumns hold: a central gutter, and both
# sides carrying real text mass.
#
# Read down the left column and then down the right, the sentences run:
#   left  : "The left column begins here / and continues on a second line /
#            and ends on a third."
#   right : "The right column begins here / and continues on a second line /
#            and ends on a third."
#
# Read naively across the page by y instead, they interleave into nonsense.
# The assertion in the test is on that ordering.

@page 1 width=600 height=792
60  | 700 | A CENTRED HEADING THAT SPANS BOTH COLUMNS OF THIS PAGE ENTIRELY

60  | 660 | The left column begins here
60  | 645 | and continues on a second line
60  | 630 | and ends on a third.
60  | 600 | Left column carries a second
60  | 585 | paragraph of ordinary prose so
60  | 570 | that this side of the page holds
60  | 555 | a real share of the text rather
60  | 540 | than a thin strip of cells.
60  | 525 | It runs on for several further
60  | 510 | lines of plain English to keep
60  | 495 | the character mass balanced.

340 | 660 | The right column begins here
340 | 645 | and continues on a second line
340 | 630 | and ends on a third.
340 | 600 | Right column carries a second
340 | 585 | paragraph of ordinary prose so
340 | 570 | that this side of the page holds
340 | 555 | a real share of the text rather
340 | 540 | than a thin strip of cells.
340 | 525 | It runs on for several further
340 | 510 | lines of plain English to keep
340 | 495 | the character mass balanced.
